_meta.description: Seven reasoning modes available to all agents. Each mode carries an activation state and usage log.
_meta.update_policy: Updated via cdi_update.py only. Direct writes forbidden.

modes.name: Analogical
modes.label: DERIVATIVE
modes.description: We have seen a structurally similar problem before. Retrieve the most similar prior analysis from the Second Brain and adapt it.
modes.activation_condition: Second Brain similarity score >= 0.75 on a retrieved prior analysis
modes.output_label: DERIVATIVE — precedent cited, adaptation rationale stated
modes.risk: Analogy may be superficial; Red-Team tests for structural validity
modes.required_lineage_entry: Prior analysis artifact_id cited; adaptation delta stated

modes.name: First-Principles
modes.label: FIRST-PRINCIPLES
modes.description: No prior precedent applies. Derive from foundational truths. Full derivation chain must be attached to output.
modes.activation_condition: Second Brain returns no high-similarity prior, OR problem is explicitly novel
modes.risk: Derivation may contain hidden assumptions; Statistician validates
modes.required_lineage_entry: Derivation chain with each step justified from foundational axioms

modes.name: Abductive
modes.label: ABDUCTIVE
modes.description: What generative process most economically explains this observed pattern? Identify the simplest causal model consistent with observations.
modes.activation_condition: An anomaly appears with no typology match in the Second Brain
modes.output_label: ABDUCTIVE — generative process named, competing hypotheses ranked
modes.risk: Most parsimonious explanation is not always correct; competing hypotheses must be ranked, not suppressed
modes.required_lineage_entry: Candidate generative processes listed; ranked by parsimony and evidential fit
modes.example: 340 accounts with unusual behavioral fingerprint — what underlying process most parsimoniously explains it?

modes.name: Counterfactual Simulation
modes.label: COUNTERFACTUAL
modes.description: What would have happened if variable X had been different? Evaluate whether a proposed metric or rule would have changed a known historical outcome.
modes.activation_condition: Evaluating a proposed change against a historical outcome is relevant to the question
modes.output_label: COUNTERFACTUAL — intervention and outcome delta stated with assumptions
modes.risk: Counterfactuals require untestable assumptions; assumptions must be made explicit
modes.required_lineage_entry: Counterfactual variable named; assumption set stated; sensitivity to assumptions reported
modes.example: If this experiment design had been live last quarter, how many false positives would it have produced?

modes.name: Cross-Domain Analogy
modes.label: CROSS-DOMAIN
modes.description: A solved problem in another field has the same underlying structure. Import the solution and adapt it.
modes.activation_condition: No in-domain precedent exists; problem shape matches an adjacent-field solution
modes.output_label: CROSS-DOMAIN — source domain named, structural mapping stated, adaptation rationale given
modes.risk: Field-level analogies can be loose; structural isomorphism must be demonstrated, not asserted
modes.required_lineage_entry: Source domain and source solution named; structural isomorphism argument stated; adaptation delta documented
examples: Import SEIR epidemiological models for viral growth analysis of abuse spread
Romer endogenous growth framing for compounding capability accumulation

modes.name: Adversarial Game Trees
modes.label: ADVERSARIAL
modes.description: Model the stakeholder and the system as players in a sequential game. Identify equilibrium behavior under the proposed metric or rule.
modes.activation_condition: Designing a metric or product under conditions where parties will optimize against it
modes.output_label: ADVERSARIAL — game structure named, equilibrium characterized, gaming resistance assessed
modes.risk: Game-theoretic models require specifying utility functions that may be wrong; sensitivity analysis required
modes.required_lineage_entry: Game structure (players, action sets, payoffs) stated; equilibrium computed or bounded; gaming attack vectors enumerated
modes.example: Stackelberg framing: if we publish this KPI, what behavior does it incentivize and what is the equilibrium?

modes.name: Bayesian Updating
modes.label: BAYESIAN
modes.description: Begin with a prior. Update sequentially as evidence arrives. Surface posterior at decision threshold.
modes.activation_condition: Signals accumulate slowly; combining heterogeneous evidence with calibrated uncertainty
modes.output_label: BAYESIAN — prior stated, likelihood model stated, posterior at each update step shown
modes.risk: Prior choice can dominate if data is sparse; prior sensitivity analysis required
modes.required_lineage_entry: Prior distribution stated with justification; likelihood model specified; posterior trajectory shown
modes.example: Prior of 8% that this cluster is coordinated abuse. Update posterior with each new observation. Surface at P > 0.90.
